facts.statement: IFSC insurance entities take the form of an IFSC Insurance Office (IIO) as a branch of an Indian or foreign insurer/reinsurer, a Managing General Agent (MGA), or a Lloyd's IFSC entity.
An IIO requires minimum assigned capital of USD 1.5 million, Net Owned Funds as prescribed, and a solvency margin per the home jurisdiction or IFSCA norms.

IIOs register under the IFSCA (Registration of Insurance Business) Regulations, 2021 and may transact life, general, health insurance and reinsurance in freely convertible foreign currency; direct insurance from the DTA is restricted while reinsurance may be accepted from IFSC, SEZs, overseas, and the DTA under IRDAI norms.
facts.detail: PO and KMP appointments are mandatory; a Reinsurance Strategy and Programme (RSRP) defines risk appetite, retention limits and reinsurer selection.

facts.statement: The 2023 Reinsurance consultation applies to all IIOs: every IIO must prepare a Re-insurance Strategy and Re-insurance Programme (RSRP) approved by its Board at least 30 days before the accounting year commences; reinsurance contracts must meet risk-transfer requirements; segment-wise retention policy is mandatory and fronting is prohibited.
A foreign reinsurer ceded IFSC business must be authorised for 3 continuous years, its home country must have a DTAA with India, and it cannot be from a FATF-deficient jurisdiction.
facts.detail: Insurance segments span 15 categories including Fire, Marine Hull/Cargo, Engineering, Aviation, Motor, Health, Crop, Trade Credit, Oil & Energy, Liability and Life.

facts.statement: Insurance sector trajectory: 18 IIOs + 27 IIIOs (Mar-25); IIO premium written FY25 USD 207 million (provisional); IIIO premium USD 302.60 million; Q3 FY26: 24 IIOs/31 IIIOs, IIO premium USD 157.38 million, IIIO USD 141.96 million, direct insurance GWP USD 9.24 million, reinsurance GWP USD 148.13 million; Q2 FY26 record IIO premium USD 210.07 million.
IFSCA constituted a Working Group on Alternate Risk Transfer and Catastrophe Bonds on 30 July 2025.
National Pension System: entry age expanded by PFRDA to 18-70 years, exit/withdrawal can be deferred up to a maximum of 75 years, and the minimum annual contribution for a Tier-I account is Rs 1,000.
facts.source_ref: pension unit; PYQ 2024 Ph2 P2 Q31/Q34/Q38

facts.statement: Atal Pension Yojana offers a maximum monthly pension of Rs 5,000 (slab options 1,000/2,000/3,000/4,000/5,000), caps equity exposure at 15% as a guaranteed-return scheme, requires a minimum contribution period of 20 years with entry between 18 and 40 years and pension at 60; for entry at age 29 the monthly contribution is Rs 100.

Unified Pension Scheme: minimum monthly pension of Rs 10,000 for at least 10 years of service. Employees' Provident Fund: standard employee contribution 12% of basic salary plus DA. Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance: maximum benefit Rs 7 lakh.

PFRDA is one of the four regulators whose powers transferred to IFSCA for IFSCs (PFRDA Act, 2013); the pension sector syllabus covers status of the pension sector in India, types of retirement schemes, NPS, APY, annuity plans and basics of investment.
